description: Transmission projects/packages driven wholly or partly by data-center load. Costs are planning-stage capital estimates (nominal USD) from the cited document; customers ultimately pay a revenue requirement several times the capital cost over 30-40+ years.

dc_link_type_legend.stated (PJM): grid operator planning report names data-center load as the driver
dc_link_type_legend.stated (PJM, package level): driver named for the whole RTEP window, not this facility specifically
dc_link_type_legend.stated (developer): project developer/utility says data centers are the lead driver
dc_link_type_legend.reported / indirect: part of a data-center-driven package or corridor; facility-level attribution not published
dc_link_type_legend.reported (partial): press/regulator lists data centers among several drivers

cost_allocation_primer: PJM OATT Schedule 12 hybrid: facilities >=500 kV (and necessary lower-voltage facilities) are allocated 50% by load-ratio share across all PJM zones (postage stamp) and 50% by solution-based DFAX (zones whose flows use the line); smaller baseline projects 100% DFAX. Allocations are re-run annually. Each zone then recovers its share through NITS/TEC charges; states split it among retail classes.

level_legend.package: whole PJM RTEP window (do not add to its component projects)
level_legend.project: single facility or portfolio; part of the package named in `package`
level_legend.aggregate: many small projects summed by a third party

projects.project: Valley Link: Joshua Falls-Yeat 765 kV
projects.region: Campbell to Culpeper County, central VA
projects.cost_basis: PJM estimate (TEAC Jan 2025); press describes $1-2B
projects.developer: Valley Link Transmission (JV of Dominion, FirstEnergy Transmission, Transource [AEP+Evergy]); designated Transource/AEP/Dominion
projects.purpose: South-to-north 765 kV backbone into northern Virginia; new 765/500/230 kV Yeat substation (Culpeper)
projects.dc_link: Valley Link spokesman: "data centers are the lead, and the bulk of those are in that data center alley" (WTOP, Jul 2026). Dominion: data centers are "a major driver" but "not the only factor".
projects.cost_allocation: PJM OATT Schedule 12 hybrid: facilities >=500 kV (and necessary lower-voltage facilities) are allocated 50% by load-ratio share across all PJM zones (postage stamp) and 50% by solution-based DFAX (zones whose flows use the line); smaller baseline projects 100% DFAX. Allocations are re-run annually. Each zone then recovers its share through NITS/TEC charges; states split it among retail classes. Dominion says the line is bulk transmission, not a "direct connect" facility, so the Aug 2026 Virginia SCC ruling assigning direct-connect costs to large loads does not apply; Dominion spokesman expects the transmission portion of residential bills to rise "$1 or $2".
projects.status: Routes revised May 2026; Virginia SCC application planned fall 2026, ruling expected fall 2027
projects.local_opposition: Nine-county coalition; Buckingham, Louisa and Goochland each set aside up to $250,000 to fight it; Culpeper officials oppose the Yeat substation.

projects.project: ERCOT Permian Basin Reliability Plan (765 kV import paths + local upgrades)
projects.region: West Texas (Permian) and import corridors from central/east Texas
projects.cost_basis: ERCOT July 2024 estimate for 765 kV option to serve 2038 load (vs $12.95B for 345 kV)
projects.developer: Oncor, AEP Texas, CenterPoint, CPS Energy and others (transmission service providers)
projects.purpose: Permian demand expected to reach ~26 GW by 2038 (about one-third of current ERCOT summer peak)
projects.dc_link: Utility Dive: demand from "the oil and gas industry, data centers and other sources of load growth"; the plan was "in the crosshairs of a fight over a data center boom" (Texas Tribune). Primary driver is oil & gas.
projects.cost_allocation: ERCOT transmission costs are recovered statewide through postage-stamp transmission cost of service allocated to distribution utilities by 4CP demand (UNVERIFIED this session).
projects.status: PUCT approved plan 26 Sep 2024 and 765 kV import paths Apr 2025; on 28 Aug 2026 PUCT approved two Oncor 765 kV CCN amendments and tabled the Howard-Solstice line.
projects.local_opposition: Hundreds of landowners (e.g., Hill Country Preservation Coalition); AG Ken Paxton urged a pause; Texas Senate members asked for delay.
